messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api-eu-central - GPU pool saturation detected on gpu-pool-3. queue_length=12456, p95=1.2s, p99=6.8s, errors=320 (5xx). Auto-autoscaler failed to scale up (recent errors). Please investigate. :rotating_light:

maya.ops: seeing the same. backlog growing at ~3k/min. some customer timeouts reported. starting triage.

emma-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-autoscale-failure. first pass: check autoscaler errors + cloud quota.

carla-sre: pasting tail of autoscaler logs (eu-central) - looks like provider API rate-limited our node create calls: 

```
I0326 12:07:34 autoscaler.go:402] requestNodes: creating 8 nodes
E0326 12:07:35 cloud_api.go:246] CreateInstance failed: 403 QuotaExceeded: You have exceeded the GPU quota for region eu-central-1
E0326 12:07:35 autoscaler.go:410] node create failed: QuotaExceeded
E0326 12:07:35 autoscaler.go:412] retrying with backoff (attempt 3)
E0326 12:07:50 cloud_api.go:246] CreateInstance failed: 429 RateLimitExceeded: Too many requests
```

carla-sre: autoscaler then entered backoff loop and gave up after 5 attempts. pool stayed at 0 spare nodes.

dinesh-ml: model-serving queues are backing up. p99 token latency hitting 6-7s for gpt-medium and larger for gpt-large. If we keep waiting customers will hit client timeouts. Can we route to quantized-8 variants for non-LLM-critical routes? That will reduce GPU memory and allow more pods per node.

lee-platform: manual capacity bump attempted but cloud quota prevented creates. I'm opening a cloud support ticket to request emergency GPU quota increase, but that will take time. Meanwhile we can: 1) enable degraded-routing to quantized-8 model variants; 2) enable request shedding for low-tier customers; 3) re-route long-running requests to the async job queue.

maya.ops: agree. prioritizing traffic: marketing-batch and internal dev clients get 20% throttle. big enterprise customers can be contacted by CS if they notice impact.

ben-custsuccess: flagged top 5 paying customers in last-hour alert. contacting 2 who already reported timeouts, prepping lines for status update.

sophie-eng: can we flip a config in edge router to enforce header-based throttles? I can push a quick rule.

emma-oncall: do it. sophie, also add rules to route requests with header `x-model-preference: low` to quantized-8 when available. I'm enabling degraded-mode now.

```
# temp routing patch
routes:
  - match: header(x-model-preference)
    value: low
    action: route_to: quantized-8
  - match: client.id
    value: marketing-batch
    action: rate_limit: 10rps
```

emma-oncall: enabling degraded-mode (runbook step 4). command: `rbctl services hosted-api set --degraded true --routing-config /tmp/degraded.yaml`

incident-bot: Action recorded: degraded-mode enabled by emma-oncall. incident severity raised to P1. On-call page updated.

carla-sre: after degraded routing p95 dropped to ~650ms within 2m, p99 at ~1.9s. queue length dropping from 12.4k -> 3.2k. Good signal.

dinesh-ml: enabling quantized variants freed enough memory that we could pack more workers on existing GPU nodes. Also toggled aggressive KV-cache sharing for seq<1024 which shaves tokens.

maya.ops: we're seeing intermittent 403 from cloud when trying to create ephemeral nodes. ticket ref CLOUD-7891 submitted. Support says they can expedite but not immediate.

lee-platform: starting manual emergency scale to dedicated-reserved pool where we have spare quota (dedicated-eu-1). migrating some high-priority customer traffic there. Expect ~8 nodes to come up in 7-12min.

ben-custsuccess: status page draft: "We are experiencing degraded performance for hosted API in EU-Central; mitigation in progress. Some requests may see increased latency or transient errors. We will post updates every 15 minutes." Approve?

sophie-eng: approve. add note about temporary throttling for marketing-batch clients.

maya.ops: taking inventory of customer-facing errors: 502 & 504 spikes correspond to queue timeouts on front-end router. I've adjusted front-end timeout from 30s -> 45s for existing in-flight requests to reduce client-visible 504s.

emma-oncall: handoff note for next: keep degraded routing enabled until autoscaler reliably creates nodes or quota is increased. key action items: 1) follow up with cloud support (lee), 2) monitor queue length + p99, 3) keep CS updated + status page cadence. handing off to carla in 30m.

carla-sre: ack. brief summary for new oncall: cause = provider quota + rate-limits -> autoscaler backoff -> no extra nodes. mitigation = degraded routing -> quantized variants + client throttles + route to dedicated pool. current status: p95 620ms, p99 1.7s, queue 2.1k and shrinking, errors down to 60/hr.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled handoff at 3067890600 to carla-sre. Pager duty: carla-sre notified.

maya.ops: leaving a checklist for followup tickets: CLOUD-7891 (quota), RB-402 (make autoscaler backoff more tolerant to provider 429 vs 403), RB-403 (add emergency reserve capacity config), DOC-128 (postmortem template).

ben-custsuccess: sending customer comms now. will update when replies come in.

emma-oncall: handing off to carla-sre now. I'm going offline for 45m. carla, take it from here. :wave:

carla-sre: taking over. I'll keep degraded-mode and throttle policy for now. if queue stays <2.5k and p99 <2s for 30m we can consider partial rollback to normal routing. incident-bot: updating incident timeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (degraded routing, throttles, dedicated pool migration). progress: 3/4 mitigations complete. next update scheduled in 15m.

sophie-eng: quick note — we should add a short-term metric delta to the dashboard for quantized-usage so we can measure QoE hit.

carla-sre: will capture that. creating short follow-up task RB-405.

emma-oncall: thanks team. good job triaging quickly.

maya.ops: closing loop on immediate customer impact: 2 customers had timeouts and were contacted, no SLA breaches yet but we will track if retries counted.

carla-sre: filing an initial incident summary for postmortem. leaving thread open for updates.
